markers.description: Mexico City International Airport is Mexico's busiest passenger hub, with two terminals in the Venustiano Carranza borough east of the city center.
markers.name: Mexico City International Airport

markers.description: This address served as a private home-base stay in Mexico City's Roma Norte neighborhood, southwest of the historic center.
markers.name: Coahuila 193

markers.description: DoppioZero is a Roman-style pizzeria on Calle Coahuila in Mexico City's Roma Norte neighborhood, opened in 2018 by chef Davide Saggio and Gabriela Torres.
markers.name: DoppioZero Pizza Romana

markers.description: Sixto Café is a coffee shop on Calle Manzanillo in Mexico City's Roma Norte neighborhood, serving Coatepec espresso, matcha lattes, and chilaquiles.
markers.name: Sixto Café

markers.description: The Museo Nacional de Antropología in Mexico City's Chapultepec Park is the country's most visited museum, opened in 1964 and home to the Aztec Sun Stone.
markers.name: Museo Nacional de Antropología

markers.description: Sala Gastronómica is a Mexican restaurant inside Mexico City's Museo Nacional de Antropología, serving regional dishes like cochinita pibil and mole negro.
markers.name: Sala Gastronómica

markers.description: Arena México is CMLL's main wrestling arena in Mexico City's Doctores neighborhood, opened in 1956 and known as the Cathedral of Lucha Libre.
markers.name: Arena México

markers.description: Tacos La Chula is a taqueria chain, and this 24-hour Calle Liverpool branch in Mexico City's Juárez neighborhood serves al pastor tacos and margachelas.
markers.name: Tacos La Chula

markers.description: Chapultepec Castle is a former imperial palace in Mexico City's Chapultepec Park, begun in 1785 and housing the National Museum of History since 1944.
markers.name: Chapultepec Castle

markers.description: Macelleria is an Italian restaurant on Calle Orizaba in Mexico City's Roma Norte neighborhood, known for pasta alla ruota prepared in a Grana Padano wheel.
markers.name: Macelleria Roma

markers.description: Delicias Mexicanas is a food counter inside Mercado Roma, a gourmet market that opened in 2014 in Mexico City's Roma Norte neighborhood.
markers.name: Delicias Mexicanas

markers.description: Mérida International Airport is the main air gateway to Yucatán state, serving domestic and international flights just southwest of the city center.
markers.name: Mérida International Airport

markers.description: Carl's Jr. is a California-born burger chain, and this Avenida García Lavín location in north Mérida serves as a quick meal stop.
markers.name: Carl's Jr.

markers.description: This address served as a private home-base stay in San Ramón Norte, a residential neighborhood in north Mérida.
markers.name: C. 29 324

markers.description: Cinépolis Altabrisa is a 10-screen multiplex of Mexico's largest cinema chain at Plaza Altabrisa in northeast Mérida, alongside a four-screen VIP complex.
markers.name: Cinépolis Mérida Altabrisa

markers.description: P.F. Chang's is an Asian-inspired restaurant chain, and this location inside Plaza Altabrisa in northeast Mérida serves lettuce wraps and Mongolian beef.
markers.name: P.F. Chang's

markers.description: Soriana is a major Mexican supermarket chain, with this Altabrisa-area store serving as a convenient grocery stop in Mérida.
markers.name: Soriana

markers.description: Once22 is an Italian-Argentine fusion restaurant at Plaza Town Square in north Mérida, serving wood-fired empanadas, grilled cuts, and pastas.
markers.name: Once22 Fusión Italo-Argentino

markers.description: Mykoz is a self-serve Greek frozen yogurt chain founded in Mérida in 2021 by Ivana Rodríguez, with a branch at Plaza Town Square in north Mérida.
markers.name: Mykoz Town Square

markers.description: Mãos Nail Bar is a nail salon near the City Center complex in north Mérida, specializing in acrylic, softgel, and dip powder manicures.
markers.name: Mãos Nail Bar

markers.description: Bowl Península is a bowling alley that opened in 2026 inside the Península Montejo complex in north Mérida, with a bar and billiards.
markers.name: Bowl Península

markers.description: Mítica is a Mérida-born burger chain founded in 2020, and this Avenida García Lavín branch in San Antonio Cucul serves Black Angus beef on brioche buns.
markers.name: Mítica

markers.description: La Mia Porta is an Italian restaurant on Calle 63 in Mérida's Montes de Amé neighborhood, serving stone-oven pizzas, pastas, and wine.
markers.name: La Mia Porta

markers.description: Popeyes is a Louisiana-born fried chicken chain whose first Mérida branch, opened in 2026 near Galerías Mérida, serves sandwiches and Cajun fries.
markers.name: Popeyes Louisiana Kitchen

markers.description: Wah Bao is an Asian-fusion restaurant on Calle 36 in Mérida's Montes de Amé neighborhood, founded in 2021 and serving pork belly baos and shoyu ramen.
markers.name: Wah Bao

markers.description: Casa Roma is a bakery and coffee shop on Calle 29 in Mérida's San Ramón Norte neighborhood, serving Nutella croissants, banana bread, and cold brew.
markers.name: Casa Roma Pan y Café

markers.description: 3 Ahhjussi is a Korean barbecue restaurant on Prolongación Paseo de Montejo in north Mérida, serving samgyeopsal, sundubu, and kimchi jjigae.
markers.name: 3 Ahhjussi Parrilla Korea

markers.description: Las Tortas del Tío Rafa is a late-night torta shop on Avenida Correa Rachó in northeast Mérida, known for its lechón and cochinita fillings.
markers.name: Las Tortas del Tío Rafa

markers.description: La Escandón is a breakfast and brunch bistro at Plaza Santander Boreal in north Mérida, serving chilaquiles and enchiladas.
markers.name: La Escandón Bistro Café

markers.description: Parque de San Juan is a plaza in Mérida's historic center, facing the 1770 Iglesia de San Juan and home to the La Negrita fountain from Paris.
markers.name: Parque de San Juan

markers.description: Micaela Mar & Leña is a wood-fired seafood restaurant on Calle 47 in Mérida's historic center, serving grilled octopus and oysters since 2018.
markers.name: Micaela Mar & Leña

markers.description: Cafetería Impala is a diner at the Remate de Paseo de Montejo in Mérida, opened in 1958 and known for club sandwiches and platillos voladores.
markers.name: Cafetería Impala

markers.description: Pedinche is a taco bar on Calle 47 in Mérida's historic center, serving al pastor, sirloin, and chuleta tacos alongside volcán tostadas.
markers.name: Pedinche

markers.description: Zara is a Spanish fast-fashion chain, and this store inside the La Isla shopping center in north Mérida serves as a practical shopping stop.
markers.name: Zara

markers.description: H&M is a Stockholm-based fashion retailer whose store at Mérida's La Isla mall opened in 2019 as its second in the city.
markers.name: H&M

markers.description: Mía Mamma is an Italian restaurant on the malecón at La Isla Mérida, serving burrata, calamari fritti, and fettuccine Alfredo.
markers.name: Mía Mamma

markers.description: Stradivarius is a Barcelona-founded women's fashion chain owned by Inditex, with a boutique at Mérida's La Isla mall.
markers.name: Stradivarius

markers.description: Liverpool is a Mexico City-based department store chain dating to 1847, and this La Isla store in north Mérida opened in 2018.
markers.name: Liverpool

markers.description: Paseo 60 is a mixed-use shopping plaza on Calle 60 in Mérida, with restaurants, two hotels, and the Casa de Máquinas gourmet market.
markers.name: Paseo 60

markers.description: Teya Viva is a branch of Hacienda Teya's Yucatecan restaurant, serving cochinita pibil and poc chuc at Mérida's Paseo 60 complex.
markers.name: Teya Viva

markers.description: Santagloria is a Spanish bakery and coffee chain, and this Paseo de Montejo branch in Mérida serves artisan breads and pastries.
markers.name: Santagloria Coffee & Bakery Paseo de Montejo
